name: Castilla y León
summary_text: Castilla y León is the only Spanish autonomous community that has not enacted any regional LGTBI or gender-identity law, a vacuum maintained across multiple legislatures. The PSOE-proposed ley de igualdad real y efectiva de las personas LGTBI+ (registered December 2024) only reached processing on 11 June 2025 after the governing PP abstained and Vox voted alone against; Vox is on record rejecting LGTBI subsidies in the region. The pending law is explicitly framed around stopping the sexilio —the documented exodus of LGBT people, especially young ones, from the region's rural areas to larger cities. For a transgender visitor the practical effect of the legislative vacuum is the absence of a dedicated regional equality office, no institutional hate-crime observatory, and no region-specific administrative protocol for responding to gender-motivated incidents. National criminal law still applies and no criminal ban or facility restriction exists in Castilla y León, so the severity floor is set by the state. The deviation from the national score (0.88) of approximately −0.07 reflects the sub-national administrative coldness and rural exposure identified in the dossier as Spain's real fault line, not any region-specific criminal threat. Compared to Madrid (0.84), which at least operated a trans law and an LGTBIfobia law before narrowing them, Castilla y León has never had the framework to narrow; the gap is legislative vacuum versus legislative rollback. Compared to Ceuta and Melilla (0.85), Castilla y León's deviation is larger because its rural geography compounds the absence of any protective infrastructure and because the sexilio pattern is regionally documented, whereas the Ceuta/Melilla finding is statute-book only with no incident evidence.

sources.title: La abstención del PP posibilita tramitar la Ley LGTBI+ en Castilla y León impulsada por el PSOE
sources.claim_summary: Europa Press (11 June 2025): the PP's abstention let the Cortes de Castilla y Leon open debate on the PSOE's 76-article 'ley de igualdad real y efectiva de las personas LGTBI+' - the region remains Spain's only autonomous community with no LGTBI regulation of its own; only Vox and the two non-aligned members voted against; the socialist sponsor stressed education-sector training, a sanctions regime for non-compliant administrations, and special attention to the rural 'double discrimination' faced by LGTBI+ people.

sources.title: Castilla y León: El PSOE registra una proposición de ley para evitar el «sexilio» de personas LGTBI+ | Salamancahoy
sources.claim_summary: SalamancaHoy (20 December 2024): the PSOE group registered the proposicion de ley expressly framed on stopping the 'sexilio' - the documented exodus of LGTBI+ people, especially young ones, from the region's rural areas to larger cities - and on breaking 'a wall' in regional society; spokesman Tudanca told the governing PP 'there are no more excuses' since the state law already demands regional development.

sources.title: Luz verde a tramitar la ley LGTBI en Castilla y León con el sí de la oposición menos Vox y la abstención del PP
sources.claim_summary: Diario de Castilla y Leon (11 June 2025): take-up-for-processing vote analysed by parties - PSOE, UPL-Soria Ya, Podemos, Por Avila and ex-Popular Igea backed it, recalling the region is 'la unica comunidad sin una legislacion propia' (a 2021-drafted law remains blocked), with the socialist delegate noting rising assaults and hate speech since the far right entered institutions (former vice-president Garcia-Gallardo's rainbow-flag 'trapo' jab); the PP held rights are already guaranteed by the Constitution and Statute; Vox voted against alone; the LGTBI Participation Council chair warned the law must not be left 'empantanada' in process.

FELGTBI+ report 'Radiografia de la educacion en diversidad LGTBI+' (September 2025, co-written with the University of Salamanca; front matter retrieved): the national federation's scan of regional educational diversity policies, cataloguing Castilla y Leon among the communities lacking a regional LGTBI education protocol.
